question: Which IEEE standard governs Wireless Local Area Networks (WLAN / Wi-Fi)?
explanation: IEEE 802.11 defines standards for WLAN (Wi-Fi). 802.3 defines Ethernet, 802.15 defines WPAN (Bluetooth/ZigBee), and 802.1Q defines VLANs.

question: What frequency band was newly opened for Wi-Fi 6E (IEEE 802.11ax extension)?
explanation: Wi-Fi 6E extends Wi-Fi 6 operation into the clean, uncrowded 6 GHz spectrum (up to 1200 MHz of additional bandwidth), offering 160 MHz wide channels without legacy interference.

question: Which short-range wireless communication technology operates at 13.56 MHz over distances under 10 cm, used for contactless payments (Apple Pay / Google Pay)?
explanation: NFC (Near Field Communication) operates at 13.56 MHz over very short distances (<10 cm), enabling contactless payments, tap-to-pair, and smart card emulation.

question: What low-power, low-data-rate wireless mesh networking standard (IEEE 802.15.4) is widely used in IoT smart home sensors?
explanation: ZigBee (IEEE 802.15.4) is a low-power, low-bandwidth wireless mesh networking protocol designed for home automation, smart lighting, and IoT sensors.

question: In cellular networks, what is the process of transferring an active voice/data connection from one cell tower (base station) to another as a mobile user moves?
explanation: Handover (or Handoff) is the cellular process where an active call or data session is seamlessly transferred from one base station cell tower to another without disconnecting.

question: What generation of cellular network technology introduced beamforming, ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC), and massive IoT (mMTC)?
explanation: 5G NR (New Radio) introduces millimetre wave spectrum, mobile edge computing, beamforming, URLLC (<1 ms latency), and massive IoT connectivity.

question: What feature in Wi-Fi routers focuses wireless RF signal transmission directly toward connected client devices rather than broadcasting equally in all directions?
explanation: Beamforming uses signal processing across multiple antennas to adjust phase and amplitude, concentrating radio signals directly toward client devices for higher signal strength.

question: What cellular architecture component in 4G LTE handles user authentication, mobility tracking, and session management?
explanation: In 4G LTE Evolved Packet Core (EPC), the Mobility Management Entity (MME) handles signaling, user authentication via HSS, roaming, and handover mobility management.

question: What wireless personal area network technology operates under IEEE 802.15.1 and uses frequency-hopping spread spectrum (FHSS)?
explanation: Bluetooth (IEEE 802.15.1) operates in 2.4 GHz ISM band using Frequency-Hopping Spread Spectrum (FHSS) hopping 1600 times per second to minimize interference.

question: What Wi-Fi channel width bonding combines two 20 MHz channels into a single higher throughput channel?
explanation: Channel Bonding combines adjacent 20 MHz Wi-Fi channels into 40 MHz, 80 MHz, or 160 MHz channels to double data throughput.

question: In Software-Defined Networking (SDN), what protocol is standard for communication between the centralized SDN Controller and data plane switches?
explanation: OpenFlow is the standardized southbound interface protocol in SDN that allows a centralized software controller to program forwarding tables on data plane network switches.

question: What protocol forms the basis of HTTP/3, operating over UDP to replace TCP and TLS handshakes?
explanation: HTTP/3 is built on QUIC (Quick UDP Internet Connections), a multiplexed, encrypted transport protocol over UDP that eliminates TCP Head-of-Line blocking and achieves 0-RTT connection establishment.

question: What network routing mechanism allows a CDN to advertise a single IP address from hundreds of global Edge servers, routing users to the closest node via BGP?
explanation: Anycast routing advertises a single destination IP address from multiple geographically distributed edge locations. Global BGP routers automatically route user packets to the nearest edge location based on shortest AS path.

question: What is the key architectural distinction between a Forward Proxy and a Reverse Proxy?
options: Forward proxy protects servers; Reverse proxy protects clients.
A Forward Proxy acts on behalf of clients (hiding client IPs from internet servers); a Reverse Proxy acts on behalf of servers (load balancing and hiding backend server infrastructure from clients).
Forward proxy works at Layer 2; Reverse proxy works at Layer 3.
explanation: Forward Proxies sit in front of clients to filter outgoing traffic and mask client identity. Reverse Proxies sit in front of origin servers to perform SSL termination, caching, rate limiting, and load balancing.

question: Which load balancing algorithm distributes incoming requests sequentially down a list of backend servers, looping back to the top when reaching the end?
explanation: Round Robin load balancing passes incoming requests to backend pool servers sequentially in rotation. Weighted Round Robin assigns higher proportions of traffic to more powerful servers.

question: In Kubernetes networking, how do container Pods communicate with each other across different worker nodes by default?
options: Every Pod receives a unique, routable IP address within a flat cluster network model, allowing direct Pod-to-Pod communication without NAT.
Pods communicate strictly via public DNS.
explanation: Kubernetes imposes a flat IP-per-Pod network model (via CNI plugins like Calico/Flannel): every Pod gets a unique IP and can communicate directly with any other Pod in the cluster without NAT.

question: What technology allows full-duplex, bidirectional persistent communication over a single TCP connection between a web browser and a server?
explanation: WebSockets (ws:// or wss://) starts with an HTTP Upgrade handshake and establishes a persistent, full-duplex TCP socket connection for real-time bidirectional data exchange with minimal framing overhead.

question: What network virtualization technology decouples network functions (firewalls, routers, load balancers) from proprietary hardware onto software VMs on commodity x86 servers?
explanation: Network Functions Virtualization (NFV) virtualizes middlebox network functions (firewalls, NAT, IPsec, load balancers) into software software Virtual Network Functions (VNFs) running on standard server hardware.

question: What packet forwarding technique uses short fixed-length labels (Label Switching) rather than long IP lookups to route traffic rapidly across core enterprise WAN networks?
explanation: MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) appends 20-bit MPLS labels to packets. Core routers perform ultra-fast label swapping (LSP) rather than complex IP routing table lookups.

question: What is the role of a Load Balancer at Layer 4 (Transport Layer) vs Layer 7 (Application Layer)?
options: Layer 4 load balancers inspect HTTP cookies; Layer 7 load balancers route using MAC addresses.
Layer 4 load balancers route traffic based on IP and TCP/UDP ports without inspecting payload; Layer 7 load balancers inspect application data (HTTP headers, URIs, cookies) to route requests.
Layer 4 load balancers do not support SSL; Layer 7 load balancers do not support TCP.
explanation: Layer 4 load balancing operates at TCP/UDP level, forwarding packets based on IP/Port with high throughput. Layer 7 load balancing inspects HTTP/HTTPS headers, URLs, and cookies to make intelligent application routing decisions.

question: What network protocol mechanism allows server applications to push updates to client browsers unidirectionally over standard HTTP connections?
explanation: Server-Sent Events (SSE) allows a client to open a persistent HTTP connection (text/event-stream) over which the server streams real-time text updates unidirectionally to the browser.

question: What is the main function of an Ingress Controller in Kubernetes?
options: To assign MAC addresses to Pods.
To manage external HTTP/HTTPS access to services within a Kubernetes cluster, providing SSL termination, path-based routing, and name-based virtual hosting.
explanation: An Ingress Controller (e.g. NGINX Ingress) acts as a Layer 7 reverse proxy, exposing HTTP/HTTPS routes from outside the cluster to services running inside the cluster based on defined Ingress rules.

question: What high-performance RPC framework developed by Google uses HTTP/2 for transport and Protocol Buffers (Protobuf) for binary serialization?
explanation: gRPC is a high-performance open-source RPC framework that uses HTTP/2 for streaming multiplexed transport and Protocol Buffers (Protobuf) for compact binary payload serialization.

question: What mechanism automatically shifts traffic away from unhealthy backend server instances in a load balancer pool?
explanation: Load balancers periodically run Health Checks (pinging HTTP endpoints or TCP ports). If an instance fails consecutive probes, it is marked unhealthy and removed from the active routing pool.

question: What is Edge Computing in modern network architectures?
options: Storing all corporate data in a single central data center.
Processing data near the edge of the network where it is generated (local devices/edge nodes) to minimize latency and bandwidth consumption.
explanation: Edge Computing brings data computation and storage closer to the location of data generation (edge nodes/devices), reducing Round Trip Time latency and backhaul network bandwidth demand.

question: What technology encapsulates Layer 2 Ethernet frames inside Layer 4 UDP packets (UDP port 4789) to create large virtualized overlay networks across data centers?
explanation: VXLAN (Virtual Extensible LAN) encapsulates Layer 2 frames inside Layer 4 UDP packets (port 4789), extending VLAN limits from 4094 up to 16 million virtual network IDs (VNIs) for cloud data centers.

question: What network metric measures the variation in packet arrival delays over a network?
explanation: Jitter is the packet delay variation over time. High jitter causes packet reordering and degraded quality in real-time audio/video VoIP calls.

question: What is the difference between a Stateful Load Balancer and a Stateless Load Balancer?
options: Stateless load balancers store session cookies in RAM; Stateful load balancers do not.

Stateful load balancers maintain connection state tables mapping clients to specific backend servers; Stateless load balancers use deterministic hashing (e.g. Consistent Hashing) to route packets without storing connection state.
Stateless load balancers operate only at Layer 7.
explanation: Stateful load balancers maintain active connection state tables mapping clients to servers. Stateless load balancers route packets using deterministic hashing algorithms (e.g., 5-tuple hash), enabling ultra-high scalability without memory overhead.

question: What network concept provides bandwidth guarantees and traffic prioritization for latency-sensitive applications like VoIP and video conferencing?
explanation: Quality of Service (QoS) uses traffic classification, queuing, and prioritization (e.g., DiffServ / DSCP bits) to ensure predictable network performance for voice and video traffic.

question: In Service Mesh architectures (e.g. Istio / Envoy), how is traffic management and mutual TLS (mTLS) security enforced between microservices?
options: By injecting a lightweight Sidecar Proxy container (e.g. Envoy) alongside each microservice container to intercept and manage all incoming/outgoing network traffic.
By modifying the Linux kernel source code.
explanation: Service Meshes use the Sidecar Proxy pattern: an Envoy proxy container runs alongside each application container in the same Pod, handling mutual TLS (mTLS) encryption, tracing, rate limiting, and traffic routing transparently.
